newsitem.title: FRANCE: Air Jet ponders transfer of hub from CDG.
newsitem.headline: Air Jet ponders transfer of hub from CDG.

text.p: French road and air express distribution company, Jet Services, said it was considering the transfer of its air transport hub from Paris/Charles de Gaulle airport to a more southerly French location.

"The idea of changing the hub stems from the fact that one of our longer term aims is to develop air cargo services between France and southern Europe and CDG is perhaps a little too far north to be an ideal location from this perspective although, we must emphasise, we may well decide to stay there," a Jet Services spokesman told Reuters.

Three sites, apart from CDG, were under consideration - Europort Vatry, a multi-modal transport hub currently under development and situated around 150 kilometres east of Paris, Dole, a little-used airfield in the centre-east Franche-Comte region and Lyon-Satolas airport.
"We will probably make our decision by the end of the summer paving the way for an operational start in June 1998," the spokesman added.

Jet Services, via its airline subsidiary, Air Jet operates domestic all-cargo flights linking Paris/CDG with Marseille, Montpellier, Toulouse, Strasbourg and Rennes, using its fleet of three BAe 146QC (quick change) aircraft.
Air Jet also operates overnight air cargo services between Paris and Liege (Belgium) Kassel (Germany) using Fokker 27s and between Paris and Coventry using a Shorts SD330.
It plans to acquire aircraft with a bigger lift than the BAe 146 QC currently used by Air Jet, the spokesman said.
"One option could be to conserve two of the three 146QCs and lease a bigger aircraft but our fleet development plans will only be finalised at the end of the year."

Last week, Air Jet withdrew its twice-daily BAe 146QC passenger service between Paris/CDG and London City airport and said its passenger activities would now be centred fully on charter and ad hoc flights during daytime periods . - Reuters Air Cargo Service Tel+44 171 542 7706 Fax+5017
